source.title: Beyond Scaling: Chemical Intuition as Emergent Ability of Universal Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
source.authors: Shinnosuke Hattori; Kohei Shimamura; Aiichiro Nakano; R. Kalia; P. Vashishta; K. Nomura

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It measures how test errors of machine-learning interatomic potentials change with training-set size, extending scaling questions to a different model domain. It does not test language-model scaling laws directly.
record.gate_note: The study reports MLIP activation-energy and reaction-energy MAEs across training-set sizes, which bear on scaling in another model domain and downstream predictive performance. Its E3D bond-energy, entropy, and representation results are not rows: they do not measure the claim's scaling losses. It does not test language-model pretraining loss, extrapolation from fitted small runs, compute-optimal parameter/token allocation, or architecture variation at fixed parameter count.
record.test_reason: In a non-language domain (Allegro interatomic potentials), the study reports test errors on Transition1x reaction properties across training-set sizes spanning about 3.7 orders of magnitude, plus a few tensor-size comparisons. This bears on V5 (scaling form beyond text pretraining). It fits no power law, reports no exponents, and the measure is error on a downstream out-of-distribution benchmark, not held-out training loss. No row concerns language models, so V1–V4, V6 and V7 (as stated for LM scaling laws) are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but the emphasis is off. The main conclusion is that Allegro MLIPs learn bond-dissociation-energy-like edge energies without supervision, robustly across training datasets (including bulk-only MatPES). The entropy of these representations explains the activation-energy 'scaling wall', where ΔE keeps improving with data but Ea plateaus. Mixing diverse data (SPICE 2 + MatPES) lowers Ea MAE (0.58→0.44 eV).
record.recipe_differences: The study trains Allegro interatomic potentials and reports energy MAEs against numbers of atomic structures; it does not use language models, held-out cross-entropy, compute sweeps, or scaling-law fits.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with predicted property, training dataset and tensor size. The authors describe activation-energy saturation on SPICE 2 and improved activation-energy accuracy with hybrid SPICE 2 plus MatPES training.

fits_no_version.finding: Learned bond-energy representations (BDE shift ΔBDE) saturate beyond ~10^6 structures. The width σBDE keeps falling, and the 2D-map entropy drops sharply near 10^5 structures; the authors liken this to emergent abilities.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Internal representation quality in MLIPs improves with data, with a threshold-like transition, and its saturation tracks error plateaus on specific properties.

record.problems: The results concern one MLIP architecture family rather than language models; no scaling exponents, power-law fits, or confidence intervals are reported. The paper identifies a plateau for activation-energy error, but this does not establish the form of the reaction-energy curve.
record.rows_left_out: No scaling-related MAE results in Table S3 were left out. E3D bond-energy distributions, entropy metrics, and other representation analyses were omitted because they do not measure the claim's scaling losses or downstream prediction errors.

untested.parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss vs parameters, tokens or compute.
Extrapolation from fitted small runs; the study fits no laws.
Architecture shape at fixed parameter count.
No power-law fit or exponent is reported; no compute scaling; parameter scaling covers only three tensor sizes at one or two data sizes; measure is downstream T1x error, not held-out training loss.
Language-model downstream tasks; no relation of downstream error to training loss is reported.
Fit-dependence of published LM exponents and splits; no fits are made.

missing.what: Ea and ΔE MAE sweeps over data size for tensor sizes 32 and 128 (only tensor 64 is tabulated). The authors state the wall appears across model sizes.
ΔBDE and σBDE vs data size across tensor sizes. This is a representation metric, not a loss, so it is noted for completeness.

record.verdict_notes: The domain is MLIPs, not language models, so all V6/V7 links were removed. The record's V7 'challenges' label was mislabelled anyway: a plateau would match V7's 'curves bend' clause rather than challenge it. The hybrid-dataset and Allegro-FM rows are diversity or reference comparisons, not scaling. The study fits no power laws, so V5 verdicts rest on monotonic trends only.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, and compute.
Extrapolation from power laws fitted on small language-model runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocations and their growth with compute.
Architecture comparisons at fixed parameter count.

Whether a fitted power-law form holds in image, video, repeated-data, fine-tuning, or transfer settings; the study examines MLIP errors versus training structures but does not fit or establish a power law.
Language-model downstream tasks and prediction from pretraining loss; the study measures MLIP reaction-property errors against training-set size.

Language-model fitted exponents, parameter-count conventions, training schedules, and compute-optimal splits; the study shows an MLIP scaling plateau but does not fit exponents or compute-optimal allocations.

relationships.condition: Reaction-energy (ΔE) MAE vs training-set size, SPICE 2 (400–2M) and MatPES (4k–390k), tensor 64
relationships.reason: ΔE MAE falls monotonically on log-scaled data: 0.93→0.31 (r2–r12, r16) and 1.35→0.60 (r20–r26). No power-law fit is reported.
relationships.display_finding: Reaction-energy MAE decreased from 0.93 to 0.31 on SPICE 2 and from 1.35 to 0.60 on MatPES, without a reported power-law fit.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Reaction-energy (ΔE) MAE vs training-set size, SPICE 2 (400–2M) and MatPES (4k–390k), tensor 64
source_check.reason: The cited values and monotonic decreases are correct, but neither a power-law fit nor another assessment establishing that functional form is reported. These results establish improving accuracy, not V5's power-law form.

relationships.condition: Activation-energy (Ea) MAE vs data in the low-data regime (SPICE 2 up to 9.2k) and across the MatPES sweep
relationships.reason: Ea MAE falls steadily, 1.61→0.73 on SPICE 2 (r1–r7) and 2.60→0.89 on MatPES (r19–r25).
relationships.display_finding: Activation-energy MAE decreased from 1.61 to 0.73 on SPICE 2 and from 2.60 to 0.89 on MatPES.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Activation-energy (Ea) MAE vs data in the low-data regime (SPICE 2 up to 9.2k) and across the MatPES sweep
source_check.reason: The cited decreases are correct, but decreasing MAE alone does not establish the power-law form specified by V5; that form is not assessed for these condition groups.

relationships.condition: Ea MAE on SPICE 2 beyond ~92k structures
relationships.reason: Ea MAE stays flat as data grows about 20x (0.60, 0.56, 0.61 in r9, r11, r15). The authors call this a 'scaling wall' and say it holds across model sizes.
relationships.display_finding: Beyond about 92,000 structures, Ea MAE remained near 0.60, 0.56 and 0.61 as data grew about twentyfold, with the plateau persisting across model sizes.

source_check.label: challenges
source_check.condition: Ea MAE on SPICE 2 beyond ~92k structures
source_check.reason: Table S3 reports 0.60, 0.56 and 0.61 eV at 92k, 370k and 2M structures for tensor 64. The Introduction explicitly describes a plateau with little or no benefit from additional data, persisting at larger model capacity.

relationships.condition: Model size (tensor 32/64/128) at fixed data (2M SPICE 2, 390k MatPES)
relationships.reason: Going from 32 to 64 helps (r13, r14 vs r15, r16), but 64 to 128 gives negligible or reversed change (r17, r18, r27, r28).
relationships.display_finding: Increasing tensor size from 32 to 64 improved results, while increasing from 64 to 128 produced negligible gains or reversals.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Model size (tensor 32/64/128) at fixed data (2M SPICE 2, 390k MatPES)
source_check.reason: The numerical comparisons are correct, but these sparse fixed-data tensor-size comparisons do not assess a model-size power-law form or establish that data is sufficient. Untested functional form should not receive limits_scope.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: Reaction-energy (ΔE) MAE vs training-set size, SPICE 2 (400–2M) and MatPES (4k–390k), tensor 64
labels.reason: The cited values and monotonic decreases are correct, but neither a power-law fit nor another assessment establishing that functional form is reported. These results establish improving accuracy, not V5's power-law form.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: Activation-energy (Ea) MAE vs data in the low-data regime (SPICE 2 up to 9.2k) and across the MatPES sweep
labels.reason: The cited decreases are correct, but decreasing MAE alone does not establish the power-law form specified by V5; that form is not assessed for these condition groups.

labels.label: challenges
labels.condition: Ea MAE on SPICE 2 beyond ~92k structures
labels.reason: Table S3 reports 0.60, 0.56 and 0.61 eV at 92k, 370k and 2M structures for tensor 64. The Introduction explicitly describes a plateau with little or no benefit from additional data, persisting at larger model capacity.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: Model size (tensor 32/64/128) at fixed data (2M SPICE 2, 390k MatPES)
labels.reason: The numerical comparisons are correct, but these sparse fixed-data tensor-size comparisons do not assess a model-size power-law form or establish that data is sufficient. Untested functional form should not receive limits_scope.

relation.reason: The study measures error versus training-set size and reports a scaling limitation; it does more than cite or assume scaling.

tranche.reason: Own data-size and capacity comparisons examine scaling in a new atomistic setting, including an explicitly reported activation-energy plateau.

source_check.notes: All listed numerical cells match Table S3; evaluation uses Transition1x structures with recalculated reference energies. The study reports no fitted scaling exponent, goodness-of-fit or scaling uncertainty, so support for a specific power-law form remains unestablished.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: MLIP reaction and activation energies across the tested training datasets
reader_labels.reason: Errors vary with property, dataset, and model size; activation-energy MAE plateaus rather than continuing to improve with more SPICE 2 structures (r1–r32). The study does not fit or establish a shared power-law form.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Reaction-energy prediction with increasing SPICE 2 and MatPES training data
reader_labels.reason: Reaction-energy MAE decreases across the reported training-size sweeps (r2–r12, r19–r26).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Activation-energy errors improve initially but are reported to plateau, so additional data does not yield continuing gains (r1–r11, r15, r17).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: SPICE 2 activation-energy prediction as training structures increase
reader_labels.reason: The authors explicitly report a scaling wall: activation-energy accuracy plateaus while reaction-energy accuracy continues improving (r1–r12, r15–r18).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
